questions.passage: More recently, Paul Silvia and Samuel Turner Jr. conducted an intriguing experiment on aesthetic judgments. Participants looked at thirteen classical paintings, six of which were calming, such as Dance Foyer at the Opera by Edgar Degas and The Water Lily Pond by Claude Monet. The other seven were disturbing, such as Francis Bacon’s Figure with Meat (the pope in horror surrounded by two cow carcasses) and Francisco Goya’s Saturn Devouring His Son (yes, a god eating human flesh).
questions.prompt: How were the thirteen paintings divided in the study?
options: Seven calming and six disturbing paintings.
Thirteen calming paintings and no disturbing ones.
Six calming and seven disturbing paintings.
Six geometric figures and seven poems.
questions.promptZh: 研究中的十三幅画怎样分组？
optionsZh: 七幅平静、六幅扰人。
十三幅都平静，没有扰人的。
六幅平静、七幅扰人。
六个几何图与七首诗。
analyses: A 对调六和七。
B The other seven were disturbing 明示另一类。
C thirteen...six...other seven 数量与分类吻合。
D 当前是 classical paintings，不是前后研究刺激混合。题目考材料构成，不把作品描绘事件当现实发生或实验行为。

evidence.quote: thirteen classical paintings, six of which were calming
The other seven were disturbing

questions.passage: These paintings are quite shocking and grotesque, particularly in comparison to the famously serene, warm painting by Monet. After looking at each painting, participants reported how interesting or uninteresting, boring or engaging, enjoyable or unenjoyable, pleasing or displeasing, comprehensible or incomprehensible, familiar or unfamiliar each painting was. Results showed that pleasantness ratings were predicted by comprehensibleness, familiarity, and simpleness. In other words, the easier to understand and simpler the paintings were, the more pleasant they were.
questions.prompt: Which characteristics predicted pleasantness ratings?
options: Comprehensibility, familiarity and simplicity.
Disturbingness and unpleasantness alone.
The number of novels read by the artist.
Participants’ ability to identify the painter’s death date.
questions.promptZh: 哪些特征预测愉悦评分？
optionsZh: 可理解性、熟悉性与简单性。
只有扰人程度和不愉悦。
画家读过的小说数量。
参与者识别画家死亡日期的能力。
analyses: A predicted by 后明确列三项，解释句也强调易懂和简单。
B 是下一部分关于趣味的方向，非愉悦预测。
C 没有画家阅读量。
D 没有死亡日期测试。评分之间的预测关系不自动证明改变任一特征就必然造成每个人更快乐。

evidence.quote: pleasantness ratings were predicted by comprehensibleness, familiarity, and simpleness.

vocabulary.meaning: 可理解的；易懂的
vocabulary.context: 指参与者觉得画容易理解的程度，不是客观唯一正确解读
vocabulary.example: The short explanation made the abstract image more comprehensible.

questions.translation: 这些画相当震撼、怪诞，尤其与 Monet 著名的宁静温暖画作相比。每看完一幅，参与者报告它多有趣或无趣、多无聊或吸引人、多享受或不享受、多愉悦或不愉悦、多可理解或难懂、多熟悉或陌生。结果显示，可理解性、熟悉性与简单性可预测愉悦评分。也就是说，画越易懂、越简单，就越愉悦。

questions.passage: In another experiment, Silvia explored the role of comprehension. For instance, participants were asked to read Scott MacLeod’s famously abstract poem The Life of Haifisch. Those who were not provided with any background information could not understand it and did not find it interesting. In contrast, the other participants who read the same poem but with more background information, such as its title and the explanation that Haifisch means “shark” in German, found it more comprehensible and far more interesting.
questions.prompt: What differed between the groups reading the abstract poem?
options: They were given entirely different poems.
One group received background information about the same poem.
One group was told to avoid reading the title under all conditions.
Only one group was permitted to report interest.
questions.promptZh: 阅读抽象诗的组别之间什么不同？
optionsZh: 读完全不同的诗。
其中一组获得同一首诗的背景信息。
一组被要求在所有条件下避开标题。
只有一组可以报告趣味。
analyses: A same poem 明确刺激文本相同。
B with more background information 包括标题和 Haifisch 的词义。
C 原文对比有无信息，不是要求所有条件避标题。
D 两组都涉及理解与兴趣，没有只准一组评价。不要补写未给出的随机分组或长期影响。

questions.passage: While at the University of Virginia, I had the chance to work with two students, Erin Westgate and Nick Buttrick, with whom I read the existing literature on experimental aesthetics such as Paul Silvia’s. We wondered if reading all kinds of books early on in life helped readers appreciate more complexity and lead an intellectually rich life. So we asked over 5,000 people about their reading habits during childhood, their current cognitive styles, and their perceived levels of psychological richness.
questions.prompt: What information did the researchers ask over 5,000 people to report?
options: Only their scores on a randomly assigned childhood reading program.
Only their parents’ political views and school grades.
Childhood reading habits, current cognitive styles and perceived richness.
The physiological effects of viewing Rothko paintings.
questions.promptZh: 研究者向五千多人询问什么？
optionsZh: 仅询问随机分配的童年阅读项目得分。
仅父母政见与学校成绩。
童年阅读习惯、当前认知风格和自觉丰富性。
观看 Rothko 画作的生理反应。
analyses: A asked...habits 是回顾询问，不是随机给童年项目。
B 当前列项没有父母政见或成绩。
C 三个项目均与末句逐一对应。
D 把此前个人观画与当前调查混淆。over 5,000 是五千多，非恰好五千；perceived 是自我感知，不是全知客观评分。

questions.passage: First, as predicted, individuals who grew up reading a lot of literary fiction were indeed more attributionally complex (i.e., able to think of multiple reasons why someone might behave a certain way) and led a psychologically richer life as adults than those who did not. Second, unexpectedly, those who grew up reading a lot of romance novels were significantly less attributionally complex than those who did not. These readers seemed to “essentialize” to a greater degree than those who had read less romance.
questions.prompt: Which contrast between childhood reading groups is reported?
options: Literary-fiction readers were less attributionally complex; romance readers more so.
Literary-fiction readers showed greater attributional complexity, while heavy romance readers showed less.
Both groups were reported to have exactly identical cognitive styles.
The researchers assigned adults to become lifelong romance readers.

文学小说读者较高，而大量言情读者较低。
两组认知风格完全一样。
研究者把成人随机变成终身言情读者。
analyses: A 两个方向都反转。
B indeed more...literary fiction 与 unexpectedly...romance...less 对应。
C 结果明确不同，不是完全一样。
D grew up reading 是既有经历，不是被分配的人生。这是群体关联，不能把阅读类型当因果或给每位读者贴能力标签。

reading a lot of romance novels were significantly less attributionally complex

questions.translation: 首先，如预测，童年读很多文学小说的人，归因更复杂——即能想到某人为何那样行动的多种原因——成年心理生活也比没这样读的人更丰富。其次，出乎意料，童年读很多言情小说的人，归因复杂性显著低于没这样读的人。与较少读言情者相比，他们似乎更倾向“本质化”。

questions.passage: First, as predicted, individuals who grew up reading a lot of literary fiction were indeed more attributionally complex (i.e., able to think of multiple reasons why someone might behave a certain way) and led a psychologically richer life as adults than those who did not. Second, unexpectedly, those who grew up reading a lot of romance novels were significantly less attributionally complex than those who did not. These readers seemed to “essentialize” to a greater degree than those who had read less romance.

They were shown to be more attributionally complex than every literary-fiction reader.
